batchName: Empire: Claudius and Nero (AD 41-68) - Easy Batch 1

questions.question: How do modern historians generally see Claudius today?
options: As a cruel tyrant like Nero
As a weak puppet of the army
As a fool steered by his wives
questions.explanation: Modern historians have revised the ancient picture of a fool and see an able administrator. His reputation suffered partly because his own books are lost.
questions.sourceQuote: Modern historians have revised that view and see an able, hard-working administrator.

questions.question: Who ended up bearing the title 'Britannicus', meaning conqueror of Britain?
questions.explanation: Claudius was offered the title but took it only for his baby son, who became known as Britannicus. The Senate also voted Claudius a triumph.
questions.sourceQuote: He was offered the title "Britannicus", conqueror of Britain, but took it only for his baby son, who became known by that name.

questions.question: According to nearly all ancient writers, how did Agrippina supposedly kill Claudius?
options: With poisoned wine at a festival
With a dagger in his bath
By smothering him in his sleep
questions.explanation: Ancient writers said she poisoned him with mushrooms, or with a feather pushed down his throat. Some modern historians doubt there was a murder at all.
questions.sourceQuote: Nearly all ancient writers blamed Agrippina, saying she poisoned him with mushrooms, or with a feather pushed down his throat to make him vomit.

questions.question: What did Nero reportedly mutter shortly before his death?
options: 'Let them hate, so long as they fear'
'What an artist the world is losing!'
'I found Rome brick and left it marble'
questions.explanation: Ancient writers say he muttered this at a freedman's villa outside Rome. As horsemen approached, he stabbed himself in the throat with his secretary's help.
questions.sourceQuote: There, ancient writers say, he muttered "What an artist the world is losing!"

questions.question: Boudica was queen of which British tribe?
questions.explanation: Boudica ruled the Iceni, a tribe in what is now Norfolk in eastern England. Her husband had ruled as a Roman ally.
questions.sourceQuote: Boudica was queen of the Iceni, a British tribe in what is now Norfolk in eastern England.

questions.question: Whom did Nero blame for the Great Fire, according to Tacitus?
questions.explanation: Tacitus says Nero blamed the Christians to deflect suspicion, and many were thrown to beasts, crucified or burned alive. Later Christians called him the first persecutor of their faith.
questions.sourceQuote: To deflect suspicion, Tacitus says, Nero blamed the Christians.

questions.question: Who murdered Claudius's nephew, the reigning emperor, in AD 41?
options: Mutinous soldiers from the Rhine legions
Officers of the Praetorian Guard, with senators
questions.explanation: Praetorian officers, joined by several senators, killed the emperor on 24 January AD 41. In the chaos, the German bodyguards cut down innocent nobles, including friends of Claudius.
questions.sourceQuote: On 24 January AD 41, Claudius's nephew, the emperor, was murdered by officers of the Praetorian Guard (*cohortes praetoriae*), the elite bodyguard stationed in Rome, together with several senators.

questions.question: Where did the Great Fire of AD 64 break out?
questions.explanation: The fire began near the Circus Maximus, Rome's chariot-racing stadium, probably in shops full of flammable goods. It burned for more than seven days.
questions.sourceQuote: On the night of 18 to 19 July AD 64, a fire broke out near the Circus Maximus, Rome's huge chariot-racing stadium, probably in shops full of flammable goods.

questions.question: Whom did Claudius marry after his third wife was executed?
questions.explanation: Claudius married his niece Agrippina, a great-granddaughter of the first emperor. In AD 50 he adopted her son, who was renamed Nero.
questions.sourceQuote: Claudius then married his own niece, Agrippina, a great-granddaughter of the first emperor.

questions.question: How old was Nero when he became emperor in AD 54?
questions.explanation: The Praetorian Guard and the Senate backed the 16-year-old Nero when Claudius died. He had been born at Antium in AD 37.
questions.sourceQuote: When his stepfather Claudius died in AD 54, the Praetorian Guard and the Senate backed the 16-year-old as emperor.
